problem:
Vantage Manufacturing sells components to other businesses and also sells spare parts directly to consumers. Its finance team wants one direct debit process for everyone, and it has been collecting from business customers under the Core scheme because that is the scheme it already uses for consumers. The result is a set of quiet risks: business debtors have a refund right the team assumes they do not have, or the team assumes a right that does not exist, and nobody can say which scheme each mandate belongs to without opening the individual mandate file.

Core and B2B differ on the points that matter most when something goes wrong. Under Core, a debtor may claim a refund of an authorised collection within 8 weeks of the debit date with no questions asked, and may claim an unauthorised collection within 13 months. Under B2B there is no authorised refund right at all, which is why B2B debtors must be businesses, why the debtor PSP must support B2B, and why the debtor must actively authorise the mandate with its bank before the first collection. The return windows differ too: Core D+5 Inter-PSP Business Days against B2B D+3.

Vantage Manufacturing needs a scheme decision that is made once per customer type, recorded on the mandate, and enforced by the system, so a business customer is never collected under Core by accident and a consumer is never collected under B2B.
solution:
Decide the scheme from the debtor type and record it as a controlled field on the mandate, not as a free-text note. Core is for any debtor, including consumers, and carries the authorised refund right of 8 weeks and the unauthorised claim period of 13 months. B2B is only for business debtors, requires the debtor PSP to support B2B, requires the debtor to authorise the mandate with its bank before the first collection, and carries no authorised refund right. The system must enforce those rules: a B2B collection for a consumer debtor is blocked, a B2B collection without recorded debtor bank authorisation is blocked, and a Core collection for a business debtor is allowed only where the parties have deliberately chosen Core.

The operational differences follow the scheme. Pre-notification, the D-1 submission deadline and the mandate evidence rules apply under both schemes, but the return windows differ, Core D+5 against B2B D+3 Inter-PSP Business Days, and the refund handling differs completely. Support scripts must therefore ask which scheme the collection belongs to before answering any refund question, and the refund workflow must branch on the scheme: a Core authorised refund is processed within its 8-week window, an unauthorised claim is investigated within its 13-month window, and a B2B authorised refund request is declined with a clear explanation and an offer of a commercial resolution where appropriate.

Migration between schemes is a new mandate exercise, not a field edit. Moving a debtor from Core to B2B needs a new B2B mandate, debtor bank authorisation, and a fresh pre-notification cycle. The curriculum should teach learners to verify the current EPC rulebook and the local implementation before configuring any timeline, because scheme details are set by the rulebook and can change.

decision.question: Vantage Manufacturing signs a new business customer that wants to pay by direct debit. The customer is a registered company, its bank supports B2B, and it has agreed in writing that it will not have an authorised refund right. The learner must decide which scheme to use and what must happen before the first collection.

options.label: A
options.detail: Collect under Core for the first collection and switch to B2B later without telling the debtor.

options.label: B
options.detail: Collect under B2B, after the debtor has authorised the mandate with its own bank and the mandate is recorded as B2B.

options.label: C
options.detail: Collect under Core, because Core is simpler and the customer can claim a refund within 8 weeks if needed.

options.label: D
options.detail: Collect under B2B without debtor bank authorisation, since the customer signed the mandate.

decisionRationale: Option B is correct because B2B requires a business debtor, a supporting debtor PSP, and debtor authorisation of the mandate with its bank before collection, and it correctly reflects that B2B has no authorised refund right. Option C is wrong because it gives the business debtor a Core refund right the parties did not agree and misstates the scheme. Option D is wrong because B2B collection without debtor bank authorisation is not valid. Option A is wrong because switching schemes without agreement and without a new mandate basis breaches the scheme rules.

steps.title: Identifies the customer as a business or a consumer and records the debtor type.
Selects Core or B2B from the debtor type and records the scheme on the mandate as a controlled field.
Signs the mandate. For B2B, the debtor also authorises the mandate with its own bank before the first collection.
Sends pre-notification at the latest 14 calendar days before the due date and stores delivery evidence.
Validates the mandate, scheme, debtor type and authorisation before file generation.
Submits the collection by the D-1 deadline under the selected scheme.
Processes the collection under the scheme rules, including the scheme return window.
Handles any refund or return question by first confirming the scheme, then applying the scheme refund and return rules.

happy: The business customer is correctly identified, the mandate is recorded as B2B, and the debtor authorises it with its bank before the first collection. Pre-notification is sent on time, the collection is submitted by D-1, and it settles on the due date. When the customer later asks about refunds, support confirms the scheme is B2B, explains there is no authorised refund right, and resolves the underlying billing query commercially. Consumer customers continue under Core with their 8-week authorised refund right intact, and no customer is ever collected under the wrong scheme.

negative.title: B2B collection without debtor bank authorisation
negative.detail: A B2B collection is submitted before the debtor has authorised the mandate with its bank. Block the collection at validation, obtain the debtor bank authorisation with evidence, and only then re-issue the collection for a later due date.

negative.title: Consumer collected under B2B
negative.detail: A consumer debtor is recorded under a B2B mandate by error. Stop the collection, replace the mandate with a Core mandate, and notify the debtor that the scheme has been corrected before any further collection.

negative.title: B2B authorised refund requested
negative.detail: A B2B debtor asks for an authorised refund within 8 weeks, assuming the Core right applies. Explain that B2B has no authorised refund right, investigate whether the collection was unauthorised, and offer a commercial resolution where the creditor accepts the billing was wrong.

negative.title: Return window applied to the wrong scheme
negative.detail: Operations applies the Core D+5 window to a B2B return that is already on D+4. Correct the timeline to B2B D+3, escalate the return as late, and fix the scheme flag on the collection so the error does not repeat.

technical: Store the scheme as a controlled field on the mandate with the values Core and B2B, together with the debtor type, the debtor PSP B2B support flag, and the debtor bank authorisation status and date for B2B. Enforce validation rules by scheme: B2B requires a business debtor, a supporting debtor PSP and recorded authorisation before the first collection. Keep the refund and return rules as scheme-driven configuration, Core D+5 and 8-week authorised refund with 13-month unauthorised claim, B2B D+3 and no authorised refund right, so a support agent cannot apply the wrong timeline by mistake. Record the scheme on every collection, return and refund event, and verify the current EPC rulebook before any timeline change is configured. A mandate unused for 36 months must not be used under either scheme.

messages.title: Collection file carrying the scheme, mandate reference and debtor details to the creditor PSP.

fields.tag: Collection amount, currency and due date
fields.name: Collection amount, currency and due date

messages.title: Direct debit collection instruction submitted into clearing under the selected scheme.
Return or refund of a collection, with the reason and timeline governed by the scheme.

accounting: Core and B2B collections are accounted through the same in-transit and settlement control accounts, but their exception handling diverges. Core refunds post as linked refund entries within the 8-week window, with unauthorised claims tracked separately up to 13 months. B2B authorised refund requests are not posted as scheme refunds; where the creditor agrees a commercial correction, it is posted as a separate creditor credit transfer from a corrections account so it is never counted as a scheme refund. Returns are aged against their scheme window, Core D+5 and B2B D+3, and late returns are escalated by scheme. Operations reports refund and return rates separately for Core and B2B, because a single blended rate would hide a scheme-specific control failure.

scenarios.given: a B2B mandate without recorded debtor bank authorisation
scenarios.then: the collection is blocked and routed to authorisation. no collection is submitted until the authorisation is recorded

scenarios.given: a Core authorised collection refund request within 8 weeks of the debit date
scenarios.then: the bank applies the scheme-defined Core refund process. a B2B authorised refund request is handled under the B2B rule, with no authorised refund right

questions.question: What is the authorised refund right under SDD Core?
options: Refund within 8 weeks of the debit date, no questions asked
questions.explanation: Core gives an authorised refund within 8 weeks of the debit date, no questions asked. An unauthorised claim runs to 13 months.

questions.question: What is the authorised refund right under SDD B2B?
questions.explanation: B2B has no authorised refund right, which is why debtor bank authorisation before the first collection matters.

questions.question: What is the B2B return window?
questions.explanation: B2B returns must arrive within D+3 Inter-PSP Business Days, against Core D+5.

questions.question: Can a consumer debtor be collected under SDD B2B?
options: Yes, B2B is open to all debtors
Yes, if the amount is small
No, B2B is only for business debtors
questions.explanation: B2B is only for business debtors, and the debtor PSP must support B2B.
